verses.text: Some time later God tested Abraham. He said to him, "Abraham!" "Here I am," he answered.
Then God said, "Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I will show you."

Early the next morning Abraham got up and saddled his donkey. He took two of his servants with him, and his son Isaac. When he had cut enough wood for the burnt offering, he set out for the place God had told him about.
On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
He said to his servants, "Stay here with the donkey while the boy and I go over there. We will worship, and then we will come back to you."
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and put it on his son Isaac to carry. He himself carried the fire and the knife. As the two of them walked on together,
Isaac spoke up and said to his father Abraham, "Father?" "Yes, my son?" Abraham replied. "The fire and wood are here," Isaac said, "but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"
Abraham answered, "God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son." And the two of them walked on together.
When they reached the place God had told him about, Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood on it. He tied up his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Then he reached out his hand and took the knife to kill his son.
But the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven, "Abraham! Abraham!" "Here I am," he replied.
"Do not lay a hand on the boy," he said. "Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you truly respect God, because you have not held back from me your son, your only son."
Abraham looked up, and there behind him he saw a ram caught by its horns in a bush. He went over, took the ram and offered it up as a burnt offering instead of his son.
So Abraham called that place "The LORD Will Provide". And to this day people say, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided."
The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time
and said, "The LORD says, 'I make a solemn promise by my own name. Because you have done this and have not held back your son, your only son,
I will surely bless you. I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will take over the cities of their enemies,
and through your descendants all nations on earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed me.'"
Then Abraham went back to his servants, and they set off together for Beersheba. And Abraham stayed in Beersheba.
Some time later Abraham was told, "Milcah has also had children. She has given your brother Nahor sons:
Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel, who was the father of Aram,
Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph and Bethuel."
Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah gave these eight sons to Abraham's brother Nahor.
Nahor's second wife, whose name was Reumah, also had sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maakah.
